channel.title: Selected papers | Quantum Research Center
channel.description: Recent arXiv papers in quantum foundations, computing, and information, with explanations of their transferable methods.

item.title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
item.description: Does including the system that prepared a superposition restore a conservation law in every individual measurement outcome, as Collins and Popescu have proposed? The authors argue that it does not, in the sense claimed. The need for a physical preparer is postulated rather than derived from the relativity of angle. The preparer never holds a definite value, so what the mechanism restores is a shifted probability distribution. A preparation that conserves one observable can disturb a noncommuting one. For energy, the preparation interaction breaks the additivity the bookkeeping relies on.

item.title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
item.description: Majorana pictured a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the sphere. Can a comparable geometric picture be given for general states, whose entanglement classes form continuous families? Projecting one qubit onto a direction \mathbf n leaves a conditional state of the others. Its entanglement invariants are the eigenvalues, called bands, of a non-Hermitian matrix L(u). For five qubits there are four bands, which meet at 24 exceptional points where the conditional state changes entanglement family. Together they form one Riemann surface of genus nine, which fixes the five-qubit entanglement class up to finitely many choices.

item.title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
item.description: High-rate codes store many logical qubits per block but make it hard to act on a chosen subset. How can they run parallel, addressable, universal logic? In concatenated self-dual codes with transversal global H and S, any logical Clifford is injected by consuming at most 9 CSS resource states. T gates on any subset need one \ket H^{\otimes K} magic state and one CSS state, so a circuit of T-depth D_T needs at most 12D_T resource states. A Hadamard parity check repeated at each concatenation level gives magic states whose undetected error is O(p^{2^L}). In simulations at p=5\times10^{-4}, this concatenated cultivation needed about ten times less spacetime than surface-code cultivation for the two distance-4 codes.

item.title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
item.description: Code-preserving diagonal phases of general (nonadditive) qubit codes can vary continuously. Can the transversal diagonal gates of such codes still be classified exhaustively? Yes, at fixed code parameters. For a code of distance at least two, every projective logical action of a transversal diagonal gate has a physical representative of finite order q, with m\mid q and q bounded in terms of n and K alone; q\le9 for six qubits at distance three. For exact ((6,2,3)) codes, 66 candidate symmetry classes reduce to 15 realizable ones, with diagonal logical groups C_2, C_3 or C_5. The order-five code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. It is also the shortest distance-3 qubit code whose transversal logical group cannot be conjugated into the Clifford group.

item.title: Tight Bounds on the Randomized Communication Complexity of Vector-in-Subspace
item.description: One quantum message of \lceil\log_2n\rceil qubits solves Vector-in-Subspace exactly. How many bits does an interactive classical protocol need? \Theta(\sqrt n) bits. A lower bound of \Omega(\sqrt n) holds for bounded-error randomized protocols with any number of rounds, matching Raz’s O(\sqrt n) protocol. It improves the \Omega(n^{1/3}) bound of Klartag and Regev and removes the total-rank restriction in Grupel’s \Omega(\sqrt n) result.

item.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
item.description: A classical f-divergence has several inequivalent quantum extensions. Can they all be obtained from one operational optimization? Yes. Compare a forward prepare-and-measure process with its reverse, obtained by Petz retrodiction relative to a reference prior \gamma, subject to prescribed averages \rho and \sigma. The minimum classical f-divergence between their complete records is attained by one spectral implementation, simultaneously for every operator-convex f. A flat prior gives the standard (Petz) divergence, Umegaki for relative entropy. A prior equal to \rho or \sigma gives the maximal divergence, Belavkin–Staszewski for relative entropy, and power priors \gamma\propto\sigma^t give the geodesic family between them.

item.title: Dimension-free marginal inequalities for pure three-party states
item.description: Which spectra can the three one-party marginals of a pure three-party state have, with inequalities that hold in every local dimension? A lifting theorem produces new valid inequalities from old ones by peeling off one party’s largest Schmidt component and applying Horn’s inequalities to the other two. Starting from Klyachko’s first-row bound, at most two lifting steps reproduce every facet of the marginal polytope for local dimension up to 4, and 455 of the 466 facet classes for dimension 5.

item.title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
item.description: Can a trapped-ion repeater node distribute entanglement over deployed city fiber rather than a laboratory spool? A two-ion node in Innsbruck entangled a photon sent through 17 km of rented municipal fiber with a photon detected locally. The Bell-state fidelity was 81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\% (with feed-forward simulated), at 0.69 successes per second. Storing the first ion qubit raised the success probability 13.6-fold over sending both photons without memory.

item.title: The Four-Qubit Hyperbolic Quadric Has Contextuality Degree 315
item.description: How many of the 1575 three-observable constraints on a four-qubit hyperbolic quadric must every noncontextual value assignment break? Exactly 315, proving a conjecture based on heuristic searches. In every optimal assignment each of the 40,320 doilies has exactly three violated lines, and the 240 possible violated sets are all copies of the dual polar space DW(5,2).

item.title: Polynomial-Time Classical Simulation of BosonSampling under Any Constant-Fraction Photon Loss
item.description: Does lossy BosonSampling remain hard to simulate classically when a fixed fraction of the photons survives? Not under the conditions studied. For every fixed survival fraction n/N\in(0,1), Haar-random interferometers and M=\Omega(n^2N) modes, a classical algorithm samples within total variation distance \varepsilon of the collision-collapsed output distribution, for a 1-\delta fraction of interferometers, in time \mathrm{poly}(M,N,\varepsilon^{-1},\delta^{-1}). The same holds for every fixed transmission probability \eta\in(0,1).

item.title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code’s effective distance below threshold
item.description: Does two-pass correlated decoding of the surface code keep its advantage far below threshold? Not with the standard reweighting rule. Under circuit-level noise some size-(d-1)/2 fault configurations cause logical failures, so the logical error rate scales like p^{(d-1)/2} instead of p^{(d+1)/2}. At d=3 and p=10^{-5}, correlated matching fails about 4.4 times as often as plain matching. Scaling the conditional edge probabilities by an error-rate-dependent factor \alpha^*(p) restores the distance scaling and a steady advantage.

item.title: Randomness Certification from Statistically Hiding Commitments
item.description: What cryptographic assumption lets a classical verifier certify randomness from a single untrusted quantum device, secure against quantum side information? A statistically hiding bit commitment that is computationally binding against quantum senders suffices; stronger notions such as collapse-binding are not needed. Consequently, post-quantum one-way permutations suffice. Trapdoor claw-free functions give an efficient verifier, and the quantum random-oracle model gives certification with no further assumption but an inefficient verifier.

item.title: Pump-Free Microwave-Optical Bell Pair Generation for Teleportation-Based Quantum Transduction
item.description: How can superconducting processors connect to optical networks while avoiding complications from optical pumping? Spin-mediated sources are predicted to herald microwave–optical Bell pairs at roughly 1–28 kHz, with fidelities of 0.86–0.99 depending on the platform. The pairs are intended for teleportation-based transduction.

item.title: Information Causality Characterizes the Set of Quantum Correlations in the Simplest Bell Scenario
item.description: Can an information principle recover the quantum boundary in the simplest Bell experiment? Generalized information causality implies the Tsirelson–Landau–Masanes criterion on the four renormalized correlators, so it recovers the quantum boundary of that correlator projection. A separate example shows that it also excludes some correlations that macroscopic locality allows.

item.title: Spurious quantum correlations
item.description: Can correlations that appear nonclassical acquire a classical explanation when the assumed causal structure changes? The authors identify correlations with classical explanations in alternative causal structures without fine tuning, and other correlations that resist such explanations.

item.title: Quantum error correction at ultra-low overhead
item.description: Can quantum error-correcting codes combine high encoding rates, tolerable noise, and feasible neutral-atom operations? Cornucopia codes reach encoding rates just above 1/2 at distances 6 to 18 and pseudo-thresholds above 0.4% under circuit-level noise. Their 12-layer syndrome cycle is carried out by rigid moves of whole atom blocks.

item.title: A solution to 2-copy distillability of Werner states
item.description: Can two copies of a Werner state yield distillable entanglement when one copy cannot? For every local dimension d, a Werner state \rho_\alpha is two-copy distillable exactly when it is one-copy distillable (\alpha<-\tfrac12). States with -\tfrac12\le\alpha<-\tfrac1d are therefore NPT but not two-copy distillable.

item.title: Quantum error correction with the toric code
item.description: Can neutral-atom logical memories sustain repeated error correction while replacing lost atoms? Twisted toric-code memories on 32 and 64 atoms ([[16,1,(4,3)]] and [[32,1,(6,4)]]) run for up to 90 and 70 syndrome cycles with atom reloading. Over four to eight cycles, the larger code has the lower logical error.
